Congress Introduces Due Process Legislation: The Safe Campus Act

I've never understood why campuses attempt to handle this shit in the first place. Sexual assault is a criminal matter, it needs to hashed out using the courts and law enforcement just like any other crime. It could easily be perceived that a university has its own agenda when it comes to this stuff, whether it's the institution's reputation, their football team, or whatever. No matter what the outcome is, one of the parties involved isn't going to feel like they got a fair shake.

Pretty stupid that there has to an act of Congress to correct this shit, but there you go.

It's because both the Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights’ (OCR) and the president have been pressuring campuses to treat sexual assault as a Title IX offense. Which means that colleges can lose extensive government funding, and can be sued by the (in)justice department, if the OCR decides they didn't apply sufficient punishments to the accused. Add to that the likelihood of a civil lawsuit if an accused is found innocent. Happened to Texas A&M back in the 1990's. A girl claimed she was raped. After a thorough investigation, it turned out that she accused the guy because they were both up for a position in a prestigious campus organization and she wanted to eliminate him. Didn't stop the NOW from suing A&M, anyway.

Colleges and universities need to stand up to this heavy-handed crap, but they're in a bad position. It will be interesting to see if this passes. Doubly so to see if it gets signed.
